explanation: Sort citation counts ascending. At index i, there are n-i papers at least as cited as citations[i]. Return the first n-i for which citations[i] is at least n-i, or zero.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) for sorting followed by at most n comparisons. Histogram variants fill and scan n+1 buckets; sort variants pay sorting cost then scan once.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary storage for the by-value citation copy plus O(log n) sorting stack; the caller’s original vector remains unchanged.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/h_index.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: When sorted citation c[i] is at least n-i, the whole suffix of n-i papers meets that threshold. Earlier indices would offer larger h but have failed; any still larger threshold cannot have enough qualifying papers. Thus the first feasible suffix gives the maximum h.
walkthrough: Sorted [0,2,4,7] has suffix sizes 4,3,2,1. At 0, 0<4; at 1, 2<3; at 2, 4≥2, so the answer is 2.
edgeCases: An empty list or all-zero citations gives zero.
Citation counts above the number of papers may be capped at n.
The number of qualifying papers can exceed h; equality is not required.
